overview: This file traces changes in the governorship and senior administration of Japanese colonial Taiwan between 1931 and 1937. Its telegrams and consular despatches cover the resignations following the Musha Incident, the appointments of Masahiro Ōta, Kenzo Nakagawa, and Seizō Kobayashi, the resulting turnover among subordinate officials, and concern that political patronage was weakening administrative continuity. The reports also describe reactions among business associations, provincial notables, military authorities, Japanese residents, and prominent Taiwanese Chinese; assess possible consequences for the Sun Moon Lake hydroelectric project; and report Kobayashi’s proposed goodwill tour of Southeast Asian colonies and ports.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Reed on the governor-general’s resignation
subfiles.about: Reports the anticipated resignation of senior Taiwan officials after the Musha Incident and assesses the likely effect on the Sun Moon Lake project.
subfiles.summary: Reed reports press news that the Governor-General has resigned over the Musha Incident and predicts that most executive department heads may follow. He believes the turnover is unlikely to affect the Candidius hydroelectric project.

subfiles.title: Despatch on resignations and new Taiwan officials
subfiles.from: Charles S. Reed II, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Explains the resignations following the Musha Incident, identifies the incoming leadership, and considers political and commercial consequences.
subfiles.summary: Reed reports the accepted resignations of Governor-General Ishizuka, Jirō Hitomi, T. Ishii, and K. Mizukoshi, while suggesting that technical and career officials might remain. He describes Masahiro Ōta’s appointment as Governor-General and Morio Takahashi’s appointment as Director General, noting Takahashi’s unprecedented effort to establish cordial relations with foreign consuls. Reed expects the changes to require the consulate to rebuild official contacts but does not anticipate disruption to the Sun Moon Lake hydroelectric scheme or its proposed foreign loan. He interprets the resignations as an attempt to reduce opposition attacks on the Hamaguchi Government in the Imperial Diet over the Musha uprising.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum summarizing Despatch No. 24
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Taihoku despatch on the new governor-general and dissatisfaction with frequent gubernatorial changes.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum records that Despatch No. 24 reported the appointment of a new Governor-General of Taiwan. It highlights public dissatisfaction over five governors in three years and notes that military authorities and many citizens favored appointing a military officer.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the appointment of Kenzo Nakagawa
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports Kenzo Nakagawa’s appointment and protests against politically driven turnover in Taiwan’s colonial administration.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham reports that Kenzo Nakagawa was appointed Governor-General after Hiroshi Minami resigned to become Minister of Communications following the assassination of Premier Inukai. The despatch supplies a detailed biography of Nakagawa and discusses whether Director General Hiratsuka will remain. It describes mounting protests by Taihoku business and civic bodies, other island communities, Japanese residents, and leading Taiwanese Chinese against the spoils system and continual replacement of officials. Ketcham also notes sympathy among both military authorities and many residents for the appointment of a military governor-general.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Neville despatch on Kobayashi’s appointment
subfiles.about: Directs readers to another decimal-file item concerning Nakagawa’s resignation and Kobayashi’s appointment.
subfiles.summary: The sheet refers the reader to file 894.00/670 for Despatch No. 2019 from Japan, attributed to Neville and dated September 2, 1936. That despatch reportedly covers the resignation of Kenzo Nakagawa as Governor-General of Formosa and the appointment of Admiral Seizō Kobayashi as his successor.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Kobayashi’s proposed South Seas tour
subfiles.from: Alvin T. Rowe Jr., American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports Governor-General Kobayashi’s contemplated goodwill tour of Southeast Asia and nearby colonial territories.
subfiles.summary: Rowe reports press speculation that Admiral Seizō Kobayashi hoped to tour the Philippines, Netherlands East Indies, Straits Settlements, Siam, French Indochina, and Hong Kong. Kobayashi would not settle his plans until after Japan’s April 30 general election and a subsequent visit to Tokyo. The tour might use a Japanese naval vessel and include prominent Taiwan business leaders.

interest: The file provides an unusually compact view of how metropolitan political crises repeatedly reshaped the senior administration of colonial Taiwan. Particularly valuable are the consular observations on elite and public opposition to the spoils system, the apparent convergence between civilian business groups and military advocates of longer, more authoritative rule, and the inclusion of leading Taiwanese Chinese in the protest movement. The documents also connect political turnover to infrastructure finance and commercial intelligence, while the 1937 despatch places Taiwan’s governor-general within Japan’s expanding diplomatic, naval, and economic engagement with Southeast Asia.
